transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-30 10:00 PT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Sasha Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (CTO, AstraHealth), Ben Carter (ML Engineer), Priya Singh (Infra)

Summary (auto): Quick review of last week's synthetic benchmarks; compare Redwood results vs their baseline provider (BaselineCloud). Discussed tuning knobs and plan to run end-to-end dataset tests.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda, go over the numbers we ran last night, talk tuning, and agree next steps. Maya you good with that?
00:12 Maya: Yeah sounds good, sorry running a bit late this morning but all good.
00:18 Ben: yep ready, excited to see the numbers.
00:22 Sasha: cool, I'll share my screen with the spreadsheet in a sec - the link is in the calendar notes, short link: http://rwd.bench/ah-spreadsheet
01:05 Jordan: ok first slide - synthetic baseline we ran was our standard LLM bench, 512 context, 1k tokens output sample, 8 concurrent workers. we also ran their baseline provider under the same config for parity.
01:22 Ben: just to clarify - same model arch on both sides? I thought baseline was using a 70B distilled variant?
01:30 Sasha: right so for parity we used a 13B open model on both, quantized to int8 on the baseline provider where they had that available, and on Redwood we tested two profiles: int8 quant and fp16.
02:05 Maya: ok good. show us the numbers.
02:10 Sasha: p50 latency: Redwood int8 avg 120ms, fp16 avg 140ms. Baseline p50 was 200ms. p95 Redwood int8 240ms vs baseline 420ms. p99 350ms vs baseline ~700ms. throughput wise we saw Redwood sustain ~1,200 rps (requests/sec) on the test harness vs baseline ~800 rps.
02:35 Priya: those p99s look much better on Redwood, is that with KV cache enabled?
02:40 Sasha: yeah this run had prefix caching on for repeated prefixes; we also had batching turned on with max batch size 64 and latency target 300ms.
03:01 Ben: the baseline's p99 is double ours, is that tail due to noisy neighbors or different scheduling?
03:10 Sasha: likely both, and the baseline's autoscaling ramp is slower so queues build. Also kernel selection on our runtime reduces attention overhead at longer seq lengths.
03:40 Maya: curious about cost; even if Redwood is faster, if it's more expensive it's a trade. did you run cost-per-1M-tokens?
03:48 Jordan: yes — rough back-of-envelope from the test: Redwood config ended up around $38 per 1M tokens, baseline ~45 per 1M tokens, largely because lower throughput increased active GPU time. these are estimates and we'll provide the detailed calc in the spreadsheet.
04:15 Ben: nice. how about throughput under high concurrency? we plan for spikes up to 3k rps for short bursts.
04:25 Sasha: we did a burst test — Redwood with burst capacity showed linear scaling up to ~2.6k rps before queueing increased and p95 exceeded 400ms. baseline plateaued closer to ~1.6k with p95 > 600ms.
04:58 Priya: what's the VM / hardware behind the Redwood numbers?
05:05 Sasha: we're on A100 80GB equivalent nodes in our Dedicated cluster for the test; baseline reported a mix of older gen GPUs which explains part of the perf gap.
05:30 Maya: ok makes sense. any errors or failure modes observed?
05:36 Sasha: minor preemptions during one baseline run and one Redwood node had a kernel retry that added spikes; we've marked those in the logs. we'll share raw logs.
06:10 Ben: on our side, our real workload has lots of long context, like 3k tokens, and heavy recall retrieval. how will that impact?
06:25 Sasha: for longer context, expect degraded throughput; two mitigations: increase sharding/TP configuration, and enable KV cache for prefix reuse. we also recommend shorter prompt templates where possible.
06:40 Jordan: also quant profile matters — int8 gives best throughput; we have a q4_0-like profile that trades minimal quality loss for big perf gains. we flagged some examples where fp16 was preferable for F1-sensitive tasks.
07:12 Maya: ok sounds reasonable. can we run an end-to-end on our dataset? last time we used synthetic prompts which are optimistic.
07:20 Jordan: absolutely — next step is E2E run on your sample. Ben you can drop 3 repre prompts and a dataset slice and we'll run the same harness.
07:35 Ben: yes will do. couple questions on the harness: what dependencies do you need from infra?
07:40 Sasha: just IP allowlist for the test cluster, temporary service account keys for data pull, and we prefer VPC peering so traffic doesn't traverse public net. Priya is that doable?
07:52 Priya: yeah we can do peering, windows next week, should be fine to set aside a 2-hour window.
08:00 Jordan: great. on security checklist we'll send the SOC2 summary and KMS notes — Jordan to share by end of day 12/31.
08:10 Maya: thanks.
08:15 Ben: on tuning, you mentioned batching size and latency SLO. in prod we want 200ms p95 for short responses; can Redwood hit that?
08:25 Sasha: with aggressive batching and prefilling cache we can meet 200ms p95 for short outputs (<=256 tokens). for 1k token outputs p95 will be higher; we can trade throughput for latency via dedicated pools and higher priority lanes.
09:00 Maya: what's the rollout plan for using Redwood Dedicated? do we need to commit before testing?
09:08 Jordan: no commit needed for POC; we can run a limited dedicated pool under a trial agreement. if you decide to go to production we'd talk reserved capacity.
09:20 Ben: one more on model variants: can Redwood automatically fallback to a smaller model if capacity constrained?
09:28 Sasha: yes we support routing policies — we can do latency-first or cost-first routing and have automatic fallback to 6B or 13B variants. fallback is configurable per route.
10:05 Maya: ok nice. any regression checks? we want quality monitoring.
10:12 Jordan: Redwood Optimize hooks into evals and will alert on quality regression relative to a prompt set; we can set thresholds and pause rollouts. Sasha: we'll include the eval config in the playbook.
11:00 Ben: about the logs you mentioned — how granular are they and how long retained?
11:07 Jordan: we capture token-level timings and per-request traces; default retention for POC is 30 days but that can be extended for paid tiers.
11:40 Priya: for the E2E run, can we do it in our region? data residency matters.
11:47 Sasha: yes we can spin the test cluster in your GCP region; that'll slightly change baseline numbers, we'll note region in spreadsheet.
12:10 Maya: timeline? ideally we want results before the exec review on Jan 18.
12:16 Jordan: that's achievable — E2E run week of Jan 10, deliver artifacts + follow-up by Jan 13, then internal review by you ahead of Jan 18.
12:30 Ben: great. can you call out which config produced the headline numbers? i want exact flags.
12:36 Sasha: sure — Redwood int8 run used: batch_max=64, latency_target_ms=300, kv_cache=on, model=rw-13b-int8, node_type=a100-80gb, concurrency=8, sequence=512/1k out. we'll put the exact CLI in the sheet.
13:05 Ben: lovely. any anomalies in the logs we should watch?
13:12 Sasha: one baseline run had an outlier at 22:05 where p99 jumped to 1.2s — looks like autoscaler thrash. we flagged it.
14:00 Maya: ok, I'd like a short 1-pager to show execs summarizing perf and cost delta.
14:06 Jordan: yes will send 1-pager + spreadsheet.
14:30 Maya: on the security front, if we move to Private deployment we'll need HSM/KMS integration and audit logs to our SIEM. can Redwood forward logs to our Splunk?
14:40 Jordan: yes we support syslog/S3 and direct SIEM integrations; for HSM KMS we have plug-ins and we can run a tech session with your security team.
15:05 Priya: we'll schedule the tech/security deep dive after the E2E results.
15:20 Jordan: good plan. quick recap of next steps?
15:25 Maya: Ben to send prompts/dataset slice by 1/4, Jordan to send logs & sheet by 1/3, Sasha to prepare E2E playbook by 1/7, Priya to confirm peering window by 1/5.
15:45 Jordan: perfect. any other questions?
15:50 Ben: none from me.
15:55 Maya: good, thanks everyone.
16:00 Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email and share links. bye.
